corrections.meaningEn: middle; half (measurement)
corrections.meaningEs: medio; mitad (medida)
corrections.usageNoteEn: Learn the middle-of-a-place use separately from half of a measured amount. The documented half-meter expression does not mean an exact or correct measurement.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Aprende por separado el uso de en medio de un lugar y el de la mitad de una cantidad medida. La expresión documentada de medio metro no significa una medida exacta o correcta.
corrections.sourceTitle: Nahuatlahtolli · Our Cornfield and Our Food
corrections.evidence: Frozen licensed source import lesson 22, section 1, body 23–24 explicitly translates tlahco metro as a half meter; body 27–28 gives one meter and a half. The separate location use is documented in lesson 31, section 2, body 24. Right measurement is an inaccurate earlier English label.

corrections.meaningEn: to teach someone
corrections.meaningEs: enseñar a alguien
corrections.usageNoteEn: In this documented transitive frame, the object is the person being taught. Learn the separate tlamachtia forms for saying what subject you teach.
corrections.usageNoteEs: En este marco transitivo documentado, el objeto es la persona a quien se enseña. Aprende las formas de tlamachtia por separado para decir qué materia enseñas.
corrections.evidence: Physical PDF page 292, governing MACHTIĀ head: nic./nimo.; the person taught is the object. The example marks people with quin- and the teaching language with īca. The licensed lesson 15 parenthetical English gloss does not establish a thing-object production frame.

corrections.meaningEn: to prepare and shape tortillas
corrections.meaningEs: preparar y formar tortillas
corrections.usageNoteEn: The documented action includes flattening the dough and placing the tortilla on the griddle. This word does not establish a general verb for kneading other materials.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La acción documentada incluye aplanar la masa y colocar la tortilla en el comal. Esta palabra no establece un verbo general para amasar otros materiales.
corrections.evidence: Physical PDF page 535, governing TLATEHTĒCA head: preparing tortillas by flattening dough and placing it on the griddle. The earlier English knead label is too imprecise for the selected action.

corrections.meaningEn: put clothing on a hanger
corrections.meaningEs: poner ropa en una percha
corrections.usageNoteEn: This selects the clothing sense. The clothing is the object; the other documented hooked-tool actions are separate senses.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Aquí se selecciona el sentido referido a la ropa. La ropa es el objeto; las otras acciones documentadas con herramientas de gancho son sentidos distintos.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF204, GANCHOHHUIĀ sense 2: nic- frame, clothing suspended on a quechcolamitl. Fresh bilingual factual labels authored from that selected definition; no dictionary example or book wording used. Saved PDF SHA256 bca334b50f02a5c83b90669007693fddcdee761fa0314616e53af6b2e79e1fbc.

corrections.meaningEn: transport a load on the head
corrections.meaningEs: llevar una carga apoyada en la cabeza
corrections.usageNoteEn: The carried load rests on the head and is the object of the verb. The checked definition describes a woman carrying a bucket or another load.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La carga transportada se apoya en la cabeza y es el objeto del verbo. La definición consultada describe a una mujer que lleva una cubeta u otra carga.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF232, ICPOHUIĀ: niqu- transitive frame and a bucket or other object carried on a woman's head. The learner label is an independently authored short statement of that action. Existing form and source-fact review remain unchanged.

corrections.beforeEn: make the sound of shoes or hooves
corrections.beforeEs: hacer ruido con zapatos o pezuñas al andar
corrections.meaningEn: walk with loud footsteps
corrections.meaningEs: caminar haciendo ruido fuerte con los pies
corrections.usageNoteEn: The subject is a person or animal moving noisily on foot. The checked entry uses an intransitive ni- frame.
corrections.usageNoteEs: El sujeto es una persona o un animal que avanza haciendo ruido con los pies. La entrada consultada usa un marco intransitivo con ni-.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF59, CACAPACA: ni- frame, a person or animal making a loud sound while walking. The new label preserves the walker as subject and does not import the dictionary's example.

corrections.beforeEn: make the sound of shoes or hooves
corrections.beforeEs: sonar los zapatos o pezuñas al andar
corrections.meaningEn: shoes or hooves sound loudly when stepping
corrections.meaningEs: sonar fuerte el calzado o las pezuñas al pisar
corrections.usageNoteEn: This describes the noise made by footwear or a walking animal. The dictionary treats the two uses separately from a person's noisy walking in kakapaka.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Describe el ruido del calzado o de un animal que camina. El diccionario distingue estos dos usos del andar ruidoso de una persona expresado con kakapaka.
corrections.sourceTitle: Tlahtolxitlauhcayotl: Chicontepec, Veracruz · CAPĀNI, senses 1 and 2
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF79, CAPĀNI senses 1 and 2: loud footwear sounds as a person walks, or sounds from a horse, cow or pig walking. These selected factual uses support the fresh bilingual label; CAPĀNA/CAPĀNIĀ striking or clapping frames were not conflated with this entry.

corrections.beforeEs: arrullar a un bebé para dormirlo
corrections.meaningEn: rock a baby to sleep
corrections.meaningEs: mecer a un bebé para que duerma
corrections.usageNoteEn: The checked action is rocking the baby with the aim of sleep; the baby is the object of the verb.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La acción consultada consiste en mecer al bebé para que duerma; el bebé es el objeto del verbo.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF124, COCHTĒCA: nic- frame, rocking a baby because one wants the baby to sleep. The new short labels specify that action rather than copying any explanatory sentence or example.

corrections.beforeEs: romper un cordón o una cuerda
corrections.meaningEn: pull cord or rope until it snaps
corrections.meaningEs: romper una cuerda o un hilo al tirar
corrections.usageNoteEn: This is the transitive action: pulling causes the cord, rope or thread to part. Learn the separate kotoni entry for the material breaking without this agent frame.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Es la acción transitiva: al tirar se rompe el cordón, la cuerda o el hilo. La entrada kotoni expresa por separado la rotura del material sin este marco de agente.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF138, COTŌNA: nic- frame, strong pulling that parts cord, rope or thread; adjacent COTŌNI has the material as subject. The independently authored label retains the selected cause and participant frame.

corrections.beforeEn: to carry something on the back
corrections.meaningEn: bear a load on the back
corrections.meaningEs: llevar una carga a la espalda
corrections.usageNoteEn: The carried thing is the object. This sense names carrying on the back; its licensed source and spelling changes remain credited.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La cosa transportada es el objeto. Este sentido se refiere a llevarla en la espalda; se mantiene el crédito de la fuente con licencia y de los cambios de escritura.
corrections.sourceTitle: Nāhuatlahtolli · Past Tense Verbs, Part 3 · lesson 16
corrections.evidence: Direct review of frozen COERLL lesson16, section2, body60 and its following person-marked forms establishes the carried object and its position on the back. New bilingual labels were authored for this fact; licensed-source attribution is retained. Source import SHA256 36711d31d650fde124cee333463b81daf63848d3ad1126d701d0003f4056716f.

corrections.beforeEn: live with one’s father-in-law after marriage
corrections.beforeEs: vivir con el suegro después de casarse
corrections.meaningEn: reside in a father-in-law's household after marrying (a man)
corrections.meaningEs: residir en el hogar del suegro tras casarse (un hombre)
corrections.usageNoteEn: The selected definition has a male subject residing at his father-in-law's home after marriage. It documents a particular living arrangement, without claiming it is a requirement for all families.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La definición seleccionada tiene como sujeto a un hombre que reside en casa de su suegro después de casarse. Documenta una forma de convivencia concreta, sin afirmar que sea obligatoria para todas las familias.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF333, MŌNTI: intransitive ni- frame, a man who remains at his father-in-law's home upon marriage. The adjacent MŌNTLI identifies the wife's father. New labels explicitly retain male subject, father-in-law and post-marriage residence; no marriage rule or copied cultural explanation is introduced.

corrections.meaningEn: carry something against the chest in both arms
corrections.meaningEs: llevar en ambos brazos, contra el pecho
corrections.usageNoteEn: The person, animal or thing being carried is the object. The checked position uses both arms against the chest.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La persona, el animal o la cosa transportada es el objeto. La posición consultada usa ambos brazos junto al pecho.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF341, NAHUĀ: nic- frame and lifting a person, animal or object with both hands/arms to the chest. The new labels describe that selected carrying position without the dictionary example.

corrections.beforeEn: it pleases me; I like it
corrections.meaningEn: I find it pleasing
corrections.meaningEs: me resulta agradable
corrections.usageNoteEn: In this present Nahuatl form, the liked thing or activity is the subject; nech- marks the speaker as the experiencer.
corrections.usageNoteEs: En esta forma de presente del náhuatl, la cosa o actividad que resulta agradable es el sujeto; nech- señala a quien habla como la persona que experimenta el agrado.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF367, PĀCTIĀ1, its nech- frame and attested nechpactia form establishes the experiencer and liking sense. The fresh bilingual label states that fact; PĀCTIĀ2 making fun of someone is excluded.

corrections.beforeEn: over there, at a visible distance
corrections.meaningEn: there, farther away but still in view
corrections.meaningEs: allá, más lejos pero a la vista
corrections.usageNoteEn: This card selects the distant place that the speaker can see. The dictionary also records a named place outside the speaker's view as a separate sense.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Esta tarjeta selecciona el lugar distante que quien habla puede ver. El diccionario también registra, como sentido aparte, un lugar nombrado que queda fuera de su vista.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF350 NĒPA sense1 and PDF351 continuation: visible distant place versus a separately named, nonvisible place. The independently authored label preserves the selected visible-place scope.

corrections.beforeEs: no soporto estar sucio o sucia
corrections.meaningEn: my own dirt feels unbearable
corrections.meaningEs: mi propia suciedad me resulta insoportable
corrections.usageNoteEn: This present first-person form expresses discomfort from body dirt accumulated when one has not washed. Its ni- composition is reviewed separately from the dictionary's lexical sense.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Esta forma de presente en primera persona expresa malestar por la suciedad acumulada en el cuerpo cuando no se ha lavado. Su composición con ni- se revisa por separado del sentido léxico del diccionario.
corrections.sourceTitle: Tlahtolxitlauhcayotl: Chicontepec, Veracruz · ZOQUIMIQUI; COERLL lesson 6
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF640 ZOQUIMIQUI: ni- intransitive frame and inability to tolerate one's own dirt; COERLL6 sections0/1/3 independently supplies the present first-person ni- composition. The existing source locator correctly claims a composed form, not direct whole-form attestation. New labels express that selected fact.

corrections.beforeEs: comer algo de una sola vez
corrections.meaningEn: consume a portion in one go
corrections.meaningEs: comer una porción de un tirón
corrections.usageNoteEn: The food is the object. This card selects the dictionary's in-one-go use; it is a food verb rather than a general completion marker.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La comida es el objeto. Esta tarjeta selecciona el uso de una sola vez del diccionario; es un verbo referido a comer, no una marca general de acción completada.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF89 CENCUĀ: nic- frame for eating food in one go or eating the whole amount. These labels retain the previously selected in-one-go use; no source example is reproduced.

corrections.meaningEn: become full of people (a place)
corrections.meaningEs: llenarse de personas (un lugar)
corrections.usageNoteEn: The place is what becomes full; the people gather there. This card does not teach a transitive action of filling a container.
corrections.usageNoteEs: El lugar es lo que se llena; las personas se reúnen allí. Esta tarjeta no enseña una acción transitiva de llenar un recipiente.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF90 CENTIYA: a place becomes full of people when an event occurs. New labels retain the place as subject and the human gathering sense without copying its example.

corrections.meaningEn: at the lower end of the hill
corrections.meaningEs: en el extremo inferior del cerro
corrections.usageNoteEn: This reviewed spatial expression combines the hill stem with ikxitlan, selecting the foot of an inanimate thing. It gives a location without naming who is there. Its component evidence is documented; direct attestation of the whole expression is not claimed.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Esta expresión espacial revisada combina la base de cerro con ikxitlan, seleccionando el pie de una cosa inanimada. Solo indica un lugar; no identifica a la persona situada allí. Se documentan sus componentes; no se afirma que la expresión completa aparezca directamente en la fuente.
corrections.sourceTitle: Tlahtolxitlauhcayotl: Chicontepec, Veracruz · TEPĒTL; COERLL lesson 23
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF456 TEPĒTL and its explicit combining stem tepē-; COERLL23 section0/body3 establishes joining and section2/body21 plus section3/body15 establish icxitlan for a person, animal or thing. Fresh labels select the hill's lower foot. The composed-expression provenance remains explicit.

corrections.meaningEn: at the bottom of a hill
corrections.meaningEs: en la parte de abajo de un cerro
corrections.usageNoteEn: This reviewed spatial expression joins the hill stem to tsintlan for its base. It gives a location without naming who is there. Its component evidence is documented; direct attestation of the whole expression is not claimed.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Esta expresión espacial revisada une la base de cerro con tsintlan para situarse en su base. Solo indica un lugar; no identifica a la persona situada allí. Se documentan sus componentes; no se afirma que la expresión completa aparezca directamente en la fuente.
corrections.sourceTitle: Tlahtolxitlauhcayotl: Chicontepec, Veracruz · TEPĒTL; COERLL lesson 23
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF456 TEPĒTL combining stem tepē-; COERLL23 section0/body3 documents joining and section2/body42–43 supplies tzintlan's base meaning and a noun-base example. The fresh bilingual labels state the selected hill-base location; no copied source sentence or direct whole-form claim is introduced.

corrections.meaningEn: hit using a wooden stick
corrections.meaningEs: dar golpes con un palo
corrections.usageNoteEn: This is the transitive stick-striking action. The struck participant is the object of the verb.
corrections.usageNoteEs: Es la acción transitiva de golpear con un palo. Lo que recibe el golpe es el objeto del verbo.
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF227 HUĪTEQUI: nic- transitive frame and a wooden stick used to strike a person, animal or beans. The new concise labels select that action; the source's example is not copied.

corrections.beforeEn: crush with a foot or vehicle
corrections.beforeEs: aplastar con un pie o vehículo
corrections.meaningEn: trample underfoot; run over with a vehicle
corrections.meaningEs: pisotear; pasar por encima con un vehículo
corrections.usageNoteEn: The checked entry has two transitive uses: a vehicle passing over someone or something, and a foot pressing something flat. The affected participant is the object.
corrections.usageNoteEs: La entrada consultada tiene dos usos transitivos: un vehículo que pasa por encima de alguien o algo, y un pie que aplasta algo. El participante afectado es el objeto.
corrections.sourceTitle: Tlahtolxitlauhcayotl: Chicontepec, Veracruz · XOTLA, senses 1 and 2
corrections.evidence: Direct review of PDF613 XOTLA senses1/2: nic- frame for a vehicle passing over a person, animal or object, or a foot flattening a small animal or object. Independently authored labels keep both selected mechanisms without importing either example.
